 Concert tourism gains momentum across Asia, Trip.com study finds
 By TTG Asia November 10, 2026 -->
 / Posted on 10 November, 2026 14:07 
 0 8 -->
 Concerts are influencing travel decisions across Asia, with 65% of surveyed concertgoers having travelled to another country or region to attend a show, according to research by Trip.com Group and Live Nation Asia.
 The report, The Concert Travel Effect in Asia , examines concert-related travel trends across China, Singapore, Hong Kong, Macao, Thailand and South Korea, drawing on fan surveys, Trip.com Group travel data and Ticketmaster insights.
 Concerts are encouraging fans to travel across Asia, creating opportunities for destinations to attract visitors and extend their stays 
 Seven in 10 respondents identified live music as a reason to travel, while 62% said securing concert tickets was the main factor driving their travel plans.
 The research also found that K-pop concerts in Bangkok attracted nearly twice as many overseas attendees as other concert performances, highlighting the influence of music genres on destination choices.
 Two-thirds of respondents considered fan communities an important part of the concert experience, while concertgoers indicated they would ideally spend an average of four days at the destination.
 Demand for concert-related travel packages is also increasing, with 84% of surveyed concertgoers expressing interest in packages combining concert tickets with travel products.
 Trip.com Group reported a 64% year-on-year increase in bookings for bundled concert ticket packages during the first half of 2026.
 Since establishing their partnership in 2025, Trip.com Group and Live Nation Asia have offered packages combining concert access with accommodation, transport and local experiences across the six markets.
 The findings indicate opportunities for travel companies and destinations to develop products around live entertainment, encouraging concertgoers to extend their stays and spend on local experiences.
 James Dick, executive vice president of partnerships and media at Live Nation Asia, said: “Fans come for the artist, but they need a place to stay, they eat out and they explore while they’re there. One show can set a whole journey in motion.”
